why: 2026-09-24 (Simon, Q5): a confirmed survey shows the customer Google's name for the restaurant, and the owner's typed name is kept as the alias Analytics uses to QUERY Places for the subject (lib/peerGate.js). The peer comparison heading, 'X against N comparable businesses' (lib/render.js), is customer-facing, so RVP sends displayName, the confirmed Google name, alongside subjectName, the typed query alias. Analytics renders displayName in the heading and keeps subjectName for its query; a request without displayName (an RVP older than this contract) renders subjectName, as before. An IDENTICAL copy lives in diagnostix-analytics/test/fixtures/. A change to either side must change this file in BOTH repos.
producer: diagnostix-proxy server.js fetchPeerComparison, called from the paid delivery

required.subjectName: string, the name Analytics queries Places with: the owner's typed name on a confirmed survey
required.subjectPillars: object, pillar key to score (number or null)
required.peerNames: array of strings, the competitors the report named

optional.displayName: string, the confirmed Google name the customer sees; the heading uses it when present
